topic: Algebra II - Complex Numbers & Binomial Theorem

sections.title: De Moivre's Theorem
sections.content: For any rational number n, (cosθ + i sinθ)^n = cos(nθ) + i sin(nθ). This is the primary tool for solving complex roots and expanding trig functions of multiple angles.

sections.title: Nth Roots of Unity
sections.content: The roots of z^n = 1 form a regular n-sided polygon inscribed in a unit circle. The roots are 1, α, α², ..., α^(n-1) where α = e^(i*2π/n). Their sum is 0 and product is (-1)^(n-1).

sections.title: Geometry of Complex Numbers (Rotation)
sections.content: Coni's method of rotation: If a vector z1 is rotated about the origin by angle θ to become z2, then z2 = z1 * e^(iθ). If rotated about a point z0, (z2-z0) = (z1-z0)*|z2-z0|/|z1-z0| * e^(iθ).

sections.title: Complex Locus (Straight Lines & Conics)
sections.content: |z - a| = |z - b| is the perpendicular bisector of segment ab. |z - a| + |z - b| = 2k represents an ellipse if 2k > |a - b|. |z - c| = r represents a circle.

sections.title: Multinomial Theorem
sections.content: Expands polynomials with more than two terms. The general term of (x1 + x2 + ... + xk)^n is [n! / (p1!*p2!...*pk!)] * x1^p1 * x2^p2 ... xk^pk, where Σpi = n.

sections.title: Binomial Theorem for Any Index (Negative/Fractional)
sections.content: If |x| < 1, (1+x)^n = 1 + nx + n(n-1)x²/2! + ... going to infinity. Used extensively for approximations and infinite series summations.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Applying De Moivre's to (sinθ + i cosθ) without converting it to (cos(90-θ) + i sin(90-θ)) first.
2) Ignoring the |x| < 1 domain restriction in negative/fractional binomial expansions.
3) Confusing rotation directions (positive θ is counter-clockwise).

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 masters the intersection of algebra and coordinate geometry. You use De Moivre for high powers, rotation theorems for advanced locus/geometry, and Multinomial/Infinite series for complex algebra.

tricks.title: Derivative/Integral in Binomial Series
tricks.explanation: If a series has a multiplier 'r' (like r*nCr), differentiate (1+x)^n. If it divides by 'r' (like nCr/(r+1)), integrate (1+x)^n.
tricks.example: Σ r*nCr = n * 2^(n-1) (derived by differentiating x(1+x)^n at x=1)

tricks.title: Nth Roots Simplification
tricks.explanation: The sum of the p-th powers of the nth roots of unity is 'n' if p is a multiple of n, and '0' otherwise.
tricks.example: For cube roots of unity (n=3), 1^4 + ω^4 + (ω²)^4 = 0 (since 4 is not a multiple of 3).

tricks.title: Multinomial Total Terms Shortcut
tricks.explanation: The total number of terms in the expansion of (x1 + x2 + ... + xk)^n is (n + k - 1)C(k - 1).

tricks.title: Binomial Approximation
tricks.explanation: When x is very small compared to 1 (x << 1), truncate the fractional binomial theorem after the second term.

tricks.title: Orthogonality Check
tricks.explanation: If two lines joining z1, z2 and z3, z4 are perpendicular, then (z1-z2)/(z3-z4) is purely imaginary (its real part is 0).

tricks.title: Maximum/Minimum of Locus
tricks.explanation: For a circle |z - c| = r, the maximum distance from the origin is |c| + r, and the minimum distance is ||c| - r|.
